name: Baza Live Chat
author: Baza Developers

sections.description:
Baza Live Chat puts a live chat on your WordPress site and sends what visitors write to the messenger your team already uses: Telegram, WhatsApp, Viber, Facebook Messenger, Instagram, Slack, Discord or Microsoft Teams. You answer there, and your answer appears in the chat. Self-hosted, no monthly chat fees, no data stored on our servers.

Features:

  • Live chat widget embedded on your WordPress site
  • Operator channels: Telegram, WhatsApp (Cloud API), Messenger, Instagram, Viber, Slack, Discord and Microsoft Teams. Pick one or several in the Channels tab; each one has a test button. Discord only receives, the others can answer back into the chat
  • Messenger buttons for visitors: round buttons under the chat that open a conversation with you in WhatsApp, Viber, Messenger, Instagram, Telegram, Signal, LINE or Discord, with one tap (plain links, nothing is sent from your site)
  • Your team is linked once by writing “link” and a code to your business account; every incoming request is checked with the service’s own signature
  • Forms (all off by default): ask for a name and e-mail before the chat, show a message form instead of the chat while nobody is online, and e-mail a copy of the chat to the visitor and to you (sent with your site’s own mail settings)
  • Pictures and PDF files from visitors: a paperclip next to the message box; files are checked by WordPress, stored under a random name in their own uploads folder, your team gets the link, old files are deleted automatically
  • Voice messages: a microphone button next to the message box records up to 90 seconds; your team gets the link (and, with Google Gemini, the words) and the visitor sees a player in the chat. Off by default.
  • Chat rating: 1-5 stars when a visitor ends a chat that was answered, with the average in the sessions list
  • Canned replies: answer from any channel with just /shortcut and the visitor gets the full text
  • Real-time polling for instant message delivery and webhooks for instant operator replies
  • Sound notifications for new messages
  • GDPR consent support
  • IP blocking, rate limiting, and a visitor activity log
  • Custom colors and avatar for the chat widget
  • Auto-questions for quick replies
  • Static mode – embed chat inline anywhere
  • Built-in protection from bots: only real visitors reach your team

Want more? Baza Live Chat Pro

This free plugin is complete on its own. If you want your chat to do more of the work, the paid versions of Baza Live Chat add:

AI assistant
* Answers visitors with the AI you choose – Google Gemini, OpenAI (GPT) or Anthropic Claude – using your own API key, so you pay the provider directly and nothing passes through our servers.
* Learns from your own site: pick the post types (pages, services, FAQ, products…) it may read and exclude single posts; it sees each page’s address, so it can point visitors to the right page.
* Your tone and rules in a system prompt; hand-over keywords and a “Talk to an operator” button – the chat moves to you the moment the visitor asks for a person, or when the assistant cannot find an answer.
* Interface texts, auto-questions and teaser messages are translated into each visitor’s language automatically.

Booking assistant for Baza Booking Calendar
* Visitors book without leaving the chat: it lists the services you allow, checks the real free slots for the day they ask about, offers extras, asks the questions of your booking form and applies promo codes.
* The price they are quoted is calculated by Baza Booking Calendar itself (taxes, extras, discounts), and a slot is re-checked for clashes right before the booking is written – the AI never invents a time, a price or a booking number.
* Payment in the chat: a payment link, or pay from the client’s balance confirmed with a one-time code sent by email; the visitor is thanked automatically when the money arrives.
* Recognises signed-in clients and their loyalty discount, and you get a Telegram message for every booking made through the chat.

WooCommerce order assistant
* Visitors ask “where is my order?” and get the status after a verification step (order number plus the email or phone on the order); you choose which order fields may be shared and how many failed attempts are allowed before the chat is handed to you.

Sell and answer in any language
* Interpreter for your team – a visitor writes in German, you read and answer in your own language in Telegram, Slack, WhatsApp or any other channel, and the visitor gets your answer in his. A suggested answer and a two-line summary of the chat come with every hand-over.
* Product cards (WooCommerce) – the assistant recommends products from your shop as cards with a picture, the price and an Add to cart button, right inside the chat.
* Nudges – the chat speaks first when the mouse leaves the page, on a long stay on the prices page, or when something waits in the cart, with a personal one-use discount coupon made in WooCommerce.
* What the chat brought – a report of chats, bookings made in the chat, what they are worth and what has been paid, and the average rating.
* Leads to your tools – a signed request to your own web address (Zapier, Make, n8n, a Google Sheets script, your CRM) when a visitor leaves a name or an e-mail, leaves a message while nobody is online, and when a chat ends.
* Let it read the whole site – one click gives the assistant all your public content, and a box lets you ask it a question and see the answer a visitor would get.

Smarter Telegram workflow and visitor insight
* Supergroup mode – every visitor gets a separate topic in your Telegram group; several operators can work in parallel, you reply inside the topic, and the topic closes with the chat.
* Teaser messages – an animated bubble with a typing effect invites visitors to open the chat; random message, delay and “remember that it was closed” are adjustable.
* Geo tracking – the visitor’s country in the chat and a Telegram note (country, IP, page) on each unique daily visit.
* Chat session log – every conversation kept and searchable in the admin.
* Cloudflare Turnstile – an invisible anti-bot check on top of the built-in one.

The features above are not part of this plugin; it never locks or limits what it already does. Baza Booking Calendar itself is free on WordPress.org.

External services

This plugin connects to the following external services. Please review their terms and privacy policies before use.

Telegram Bot API (api.telegram.org)

Used when you set up Telegram as an operator channel (the chat needs at least one channel). Every visitor message and operator reply is then transmitted through Telegram’s servers using the bot token you configure.
* Terms of Service: https://telegram.org/tos
* Privacy Policy: https://telegram.org/privacy

Slack (slack.com), Discord (discord.com) and Microsoft Teams (optional)

Only if you enter that service’s credentials in Baza Live Chat > Channels. Then every chat message (the visitor’s text, the visitor’s country, IP address and page when a chat starts) is sent to the Slack channel, Discord channel or Teams channel you chose, through that service’s official address: https://slack.com/api/chat.postMessage, the Discord webhook URL you created (discord.com/api/webhooks/…) and the Teams workflow webhook URL you created. Answers written in Slack or Teams reach your site through addresses of your own site that are accepted only with that service’s signature (Slack signing secret, Teams security token). Nothing is sent to these services while their fields are empty.
* Slack: https://slack.com/terms-of-service and https://slack.com/trust/privacy/privacy-policy
* Discord: https://discord.com/terms and https://discord.com/privacy
* Microsoft Teams: https://www.microsoft.com/servicesagreement and https://privacy.microsoft.com/privacystatement

WhatsApp Cloud API, Facebook Messenger and Instagram (Meta) and Viber (optional)

Only if you enter that service’s credentials in Baza Live Chat > Channels. Chat events (the visitor’s text; the country, IP address and page when a chat starts) are then sent to the people of your team that you linked, through the official addresses https://graph.facebook.com (WhatsApp Cloud API, Messenger and Instagram Messaging) and https://chatapi.viber.com. Answers reach your site through addresses of your own site that accept only requests signed by the service (Meta: the app secret; Viber: the bot token). Only the linked people are listened to. Nothing is sent while the fields are empty.
* Meta (WhatsApp, Messenger, Instagram): https://www.whatsapp.com/legal/business-terms, https://developers.facebook.com/terms and https://www.facebook.com/privacy/policy
* Viber: https://www.viber.com/en/terms/viber-terms-use/ and https://www.viber.com/en/terms/viber-privacy-policy/

Messenger buttons (WhatsApp, Viber, Messenger, Instagram, Telegram, Signal, LINE, Discord)

Optional. When you enter an account for a messenger in Baza Live Chat > Messengers, the chat window shows a round button that is a plain link to that messenger’s public “write to us” address (wa.me, viber://, m.me, ig.me, t.me, signal.me, line.me or your Discord invite). The plugin sends nothing to these services and loads no script from them: they are contacted only when a visitor clicks a button, and then under the terms of that service.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin files to /wp-content/plugins/baza-live-chat/ or install via the WordPress plugin screen.
  2. Activate the plugin through the Plugins screen in WordPress.
  3. Go to Baza Live Chat → Channels and pick a messenger. For Telegram: create a bot via @BotFather, enter its Bot Token and your Chat ID, click Save, then Set Webhook. The other messengers have their own steps under the field names.
  4. Optional: in Messengers, add your WhatsApp number or other accounts to show contact buttons under the chat.
  5. The chat widget will appear on your site automatically.
sections.faq:
Do I need a paid account?

No. Everything in this plugin is free. You only need one channel that your team reads, for example a Telegram bot (free to create with @BotFather). WhatsApp, Messenger, Instagram and Viber need an account of that service for business, and the service may charge for it. A paid Pro version with extra features (AI assistant with Gemini, OpenAI or Claude, a booking assistant for Baza Booking Calendar, WooCommerce order lookup, Supergroup mode and more) is available at bazadevelopers.com, see the list in the description.

Is it safe to let visitors send files?

Only JPG, PNG, GIF, WebP and PDF are accepted, the type is checked by WordPress itself (not just the file name), the size limit is yours to set (5 MB by default), and each file is saved under a random name in wp-content/uploads/baza-live-chat/ where scripts cannot run. Files older than the number of days you choose are deleted by a daily task. The option is off until you turn it on in Forms.

How do canned replies work?

In Forms → Canned replies write one per line: hi | Hello! How can I help you?. When you answer a chat from Telegram, Slack, Teams or another channel with only /hi, the visitor receives the text.

Is my data stored on your servers?

No. All chat data is stored in your own WordPress database. Messages go directly from your site to the channels you set up, for example your Telegram bot.

Does it work with page builders?

Yes. Use the [baza_live_chat] shortcode to embed the chat anywhere, including Gutenberg, Elementor, and other page builders. Add static="true" to show it as an inline block.

Where is the readable source of the minified scripts?

In the plugin itself: every *.min.js in assets/js/ sits next to the file of the same name without .min. They are generated with Terser (npx terser blc.js -c -m -o blc.min.js).
sections.changelog:
1.6.1

  • New: voice messages (a microphone button next to the message box, up to 90 seconds, a player in the chat); the team is told at once and a recording that holds only silence is not sent.
  • New: the language of the plugin’s screens in the admin can be set in the address: &lang=en (also ru, uk, de, pl, sk, pt; &lang=default goes back).
  • Changed: the Channels tab shows all the messengers at once as tiles, with a dot on the ones that are set up.
  • Changed: a wider chat window, a one-line placeholder and a tighter line height in the message box, the star of the rating is an SVG.
  • Changed: spacing, font sizes and radii of the chat and the admin come from root CSS variables.
  • Fixed: a file sent by a visitor ran the server out of memory on some sites; files are shown as links (not as raw markers) in the sessions list and in e-mailed copies of a chat.

1.6.0

  • Changed: quieter admin screens: actions that sit next to a value (make a new code, unlink all) are plain text links instead of grey buttons, and long explanations keep a comfortable line length.
  • Pro: interpreter for the team, product cards, nudges with coupon, report “What the chat brought”, one-click site knowledge (see the list above).

1.5.0

  • New: Slack, Discord and Microsoft Teams as operator channels besides Telegram. The messages of the chat (and, in the Pro build, new orders and bookings made in the chat) are also sent to the channels you set up (a “Slack, Discord, Teams” tab, with a test button for each); answers written in the Slack thread of a chat, or in Teams with the code of the chat, go back into the chat. Discord only receives. The chat can now run without Telegram when one of these is set up. Every incoming request is checked with the service’s own signature.
  • New: WhatsApp (Cloud API), Facebook Messenger, Instagram and Viber as operator channels. A person of your team is linked once by writing “link CODE” to your business account; the chat messages then come to them in that messenger, and they answer by replying to a message, by starting with session:CODE, or (Viber) simply by answering. Webhooks are accepted only with the service’s signature, and only from linked people.
  • New: messenger buttons in the chat window. A “Messengers” tab takes a phone number or an account name for WhatsApp, Viber, Messenger, Instagram, Telegram, Signal, LINE and Discord; each one becomes a round button under the chat that opens a conversation with you in the visitor’s own messenger. They are plain links, nothing is sent to those services from your site.
  • New: a “Forms” tab. An optional pre-chat form asks for name and e-mail (off, optional or required) before a chat starts; both are shown to your team in the first message. An optional offline message form replaces the chat outside working hours and sends the message to your e-mail address (and to Telegram) with a honeypot and rate limit. Visitors can have a copy of the chat sent to their e-mail, and you can receive a copy of every closed chat. All e-mails go through wp_mail() of your own site; no external service is involved, and all of it is off by default.
  • New: pictures and PDF files from visitors. A paperclip next to the message box sends a JPG, PNG, GIF, WebP or PDF (size limit you set, 5 MB by default); the file is checked by WordPress, stored in its own folder of your uploads directory under a random name, shown in the chat, and your team receives the link. Old files are deleted by a daily task. Off by default.
  • New: chat rating. When a visitor ends a chat that was answered, 1-5 stars are offered; the rating goes to your channels and the sessions list shows the average. Off by default.
  • New: canned replies. Write one per line (shortcut | text) and answer a chat from Telegram, Slack, Teams or another channel with just /shortcut.
  • Fixed: the chat window clips its header and body to a single radius (no hairline at the corners on dark pages), and the privacy notice no longer inherits a white text colour from dark sites.

1.3.3

  • Fixed: pages could not be cached by page-cache plugins and server caches (and cache warm-ups reported “response-sets-cookie”), because the visitor cookie was set in the page’s own response. The cookie is now set in the browser, once a real person has been seen, and the page itself sets no cookie.

1.3.2

  • Only real visitors reach your Telegram. A visit is reported, and a chat can be started, only by a browser that passes a quiet check: the request must look like a visitor’s browser (crawlers, headless browsers, HTTP libraries, AI and SEO bots, link previews and speed tests are refused by name; calls from other sites are refused), the page does a small proof-of-work in the background (about a tenth of a second, once), and a visit is reported only after a real mouse, key, touch or scroll event and a moment on screen.
  • The visitor’s address is no longer taken from headers anyone can write (Client-IP, X-Forwarded-For): they are read only behind a reverse proxy you run or Cloudflare, so per-address limits and IP blocks cannot be sidestepped. Extra trusted proxies: the filter baza_lc_trusted_proxies.
  • The visit counter asks “was this address already counted today?” before it spends a rate-limit write.

1.3.1

  • A “Get Pro” button in the plugin’s header and an “Upgrade to Pro” item at the bottom of its menu; both are plain links to the plugin’s page and can be turned off.
